# 4 Maccabees Chapter 18 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Sinaiticus) | **Section:** Conclusion: Epilogue of Praise

---

**1** O children of Israel, offspring of the seed of Abraham, obey this law and exercise piety in every way,

**2** knowing that devout reason is master of all the passions, not only of those that arise from within but also of those that come from without.

**3** For this reason those men surrendered their bodies to the pain of torments for the sake of God.

**4** And it was through the blood of those devout ones and their death as an atoning sacrifice that divine providence preserved Israel, which had previously been afflicted.

**5** For the tyrant Antiochus, when he saw the courage of their virtue and their patient endurance under the tortures, proclaimed them to his soldiers as an example of endurance.

**6** And this made them ashamed and courageous in battle and patient endurance, so that the enemy was unable to subdue the nation even by force and abandoned the attempt.

**7** Thus through the nobility of those who died for God, reason is proved to be sovereign over the passions.

**8** But it would be wrong for me not to recall also the courage of the mother as being worthy of more than mere praise.

**9** For though she watched seven sons die within the space of one day, she endured this heroically because of her hope in God.

**10** She exhorted each of them in the language of their fathers, being filled with a noble spirit.

**11** She said to them: My sons, I brought you forth from the womb; I nursed you for three years; I raised you and brought you to the place you stand today.

**12** I urge you, my children, to look at the heaven and the earth and all that is in them, and to know that God made them out of nothing, and that the human race came into being in the same way.

**13** Do not be afraid of this tormentor, but be worthy of your brothers.

**14** Accept death, so that in God's mercy I may receive you again with your brothers.

**15** While she was yet speaking, the youngest son spoke up and said: O guardians of the law, O friends of virtue, death holds no terror for those who live in accordance with virtue.

**16** This most holy and pious mother, filled with joy at the noble deaths of her sons and not overcome with grief at their passing, urged them on to die for the sake of God, saying to each of them:

**17** Be courageous, my children! Do not fear death! If you remain faithful to the law, God will grant you a glorious resurrection.

**18** She herself then put the seal on her own faithfulness by following her sons in death.

**19** And I call blessed and holy all those who died in this manner for the sake of God.

**20** For they overcame the tyrant by their patient endurance, and through them their nation was purified.

**21** Let us therefore conclude with this: devout reason is the sovereign master of the passions, as the examples of Eleazar, the seven brothers, and the mother have demonstrated.

**22** They overcame the passions; they conquered the tyrant; they have won the prizes of immortality.

**23** They were righteous, and they kept faith with God in life and in death.

**24** Blessed indeed and most holy are the memories of Eleazar, the seven brothers, and the mother, for they fought for the honor of God.

**25** And their souls are now with God, who will honor them forever.
